hints: Notice the field strength $3.0 \times 10^7$ $\text{N C}^{-1}$ is already given, so you do not need the distance or Coulomb's law with the alpha charge.
Recall that field strength is force per unit charge, $E = F/Q$, so the force on the electron is $F = EQ$ with $Q$ the electron charge.
Use magnitude $Q = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}$ $\text{C}$ for the electron and check the power of ten when multiplying by $10^7$.
walkthrough: Identify the given field $E = 3.0 \times 10^7$ $\text{N C}^{-1}$ at the electron position and the charge experiencing it, the electron with magnitude $Q = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}$ $\text{C}$.
State the governing relation: electric field strength is force per charge, $E = F/Q$, so $F = EQ$.
Substitute values with units: $F = (3.0 \times 10^7 \text{ N C}^{-1})(1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C})$.
Calculate magnitude: $3.0 \times 1.6 = 4.8$ and $10^7 \times 10^{-19} = 10^{-12}$, giving $F = 4.8 \times 10^{-12}$ $\text{N}$ attractive toward the positive alpha particle.
